questions.q: Who does David say speaks lies against him?
questions.a: David says that wicked and deceitful people speak lies about him.

questions.q: What do the wicked give in return for David’s love?
questions.a: David says that in return for his love, they accuse him of doing evil things.

questions.q: What does David hope will happen when his enemy is judged?
questions.a: David hopes that when his enemy is judged, he may be found guilty.

questions.q: What is David’s request for the children of his enemy?
questions.a: David asks that his enemy’s children would have to wander about and beg for food.

questions.q: What does David hope will happen to his enemy’s earnings?
questions.a: David hopes that strangers will take what his enemy earns.

questions.q: What does David hope regarding his enemy and his enemy’s children?
questions.a: David hopes that no one will show covenant faithfulness to his enemy and that no one will pity his enemy’s fatherless children.

questions.q: What is David’s request from Yahweh concerning his enemy?
questions.a: David asks that Yahweh will cause everyone on earth to completely forget who they were.

questions.q: Why does David ask Yahweh to make sure no one remembers his enemy?
questions.a: David asks this because his enemy persecuted poor, needy, and brokenhearted people until they died.

questions.q: What does David say about his enemy’s attitude toward cursing and blessing?
questions.a: David says that because his enemy loved to curse others, now people are cursing him, and because his enemy did not bless others, there will be no one who blesses him.

questions.q: What does David ask Yahweh to do for him, and why?
questions.a: David asks Yahweh to be kind to him for the sake of Yahweh’s name and to rescue him because of the promise Yahweh made to faithfully love him.

questions.q: To what does David compare his time left to remain alive?
questions.a: David says that his life is fading away as quickly as a shadow that lengthens at evening or as a man shakes off a locust.

questions.q: What do David’s accusers do when they see him?
questions.a: David says that when they see him, his accusers shake their heads to show that they despise him.

questions.q: What does David say will be the result of Yahweh saving him?
questions.a: When Yahweh saves him, his enemies will know that it was Yahweh who has done it.

questions.q: Why does David think Yahweh will save him?
questions.a: David asks Yahweh to save him because Yahweh has faithfully loved him according to his covenant.

questions.q: What does David say will happen when his accusers curse him?
questions.a: David says that when his accusers curse him, Yahweh will bless him and cause him to rejoice.

questions.q: What does David say will happen when Yahweh defends the needy person?
questions.a: Yahweh will save the needy person from those who condemn him.

commentary.text: Verses 1–5 It is the unspeakable comfort of all believers, that whoever is against them, God is for them; and to him they may apply as to one pleased to concern himself for them. David's enemies laughed at him for his devotion, but they could not laugh him out of it.

The Lord Jesus may speak here as a Judge, denouncing sentence on some of his enemies, to warn others. When men reject the salvation of Christ, even their prayers are numbered among their sins. See what hurries some to shameful deaths, and brings the families and estates of others to ruin; makes them and theirs despicable and hateful, and brings poverty, shame, and misery upon their posterity: it is sin, that mischievous, destructive thing. And what will be the effect of the sentence, “Go, ye cursed,” upon the bodies and souls of the wicked! How it will affect the senses of the body, and the powers of the soul, with pain, anguish, horror, and despair! Think on these things, sinners, tremble and repent.

The psalmist takes God's comforts to himself, but in a very humble manner. He was troubled in mind. His body was wasted, and almost worn away. But it is better to have leanness in the body, while the soul prospers and is in health, than to have leanness in the soul, while the body is feasted. He was ridiculed and reproached by his enemies. But if God bless us, we need not care who curses us; for how can they curse whom God has not cursed; nay, whom he has blessed? He pleads God's glory, and the honour of his name. Save me, not according to my merit, for I pretend to none, but according to thy-mercy. He concludes with the joy of faith, in assurance that his present conflicts would end in triumphs. Let all that suffer according to the will of God, commit the keeping of their souls to him. Jesus, unjustly put to death, and now risen again, is an Advocate and Intercessor for his people, ever ready to appear on their behalf against a corrupt world, and the great accuser.
